clue.text: Support clubs in remote region

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
woods are a kind of golf club

explanation.surface: A rural team gets help from local sports clubs out in the sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' tempts you toward the card suit (C), but here it means golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The backwoods are sparsely populated, isolated country far from towns.

clue.text: Carries family hat worn on ceremonial occasions

parts.note: to bear is to carry
kin are relatives, family

explanation.surface: A family member carries the ceremonial headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is the tall black fur cap worn by British Guards regiments, as seen outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearskin is the tall fur cap worn by guardsmen on ceremonial duty.

clue.text: Plant initially consumed colony of bees

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of consumed
a hive is a bee colony

explanation.surface: A plant was first eaten by a swarm of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Chives are a herb, a small onion-flavoured plant.

clue.text: Whiskey cooler photographer gives young rascal

parts.note: W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hipper means more fashionable, cooler
a snapper is informal for a photographer

explanation.surface: A trendier photographer hands whisky to a cheeky youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a fridge or ice bucket for the whiskey, but it means more fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impertinent or presumptuous young person.

clue.text: Active regarding getting article ready

parts.note: on can mean about or regarding
the definite article
go as an adjective means ready, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: Someone busy is preparing an item about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the go is to be busy and constantly active.

clue.text: Turned over rugs in academy showing endurance

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so it reads the other way

parts.note: mats are small rugs
taken as written
A is a common abbreviation for academy

explanation.surface: Someone shows real staying power flipping rugs over at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental strength to keep going, which is endurance.

clue.text: Snub I assume hides prejudice

indicators.note: something that hides another keeps it tucked away inside, so the answer sits within the neighbouring words

parts.note: found running across snuB I ASsume

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a cold shoulder conceals a prejudiced attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair leaning for or against something, the same as a preconceived judgement.

clue.text: Chimney in pub by church produces effect

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a flue is a chimney duct
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chimney in the pub next to the church makes its presence felt.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence and effect both name the power one thing has to change another.

clue.text: Son first to meet Virgin Queen and nun

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
1st written with I for the figure 1
Elizabeth I was the Virgin Queen, and ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A boy is first in line to be presented to Elizabeth I alongside a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is written as the ordinal 1ST with the digit read as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister is the title used for a nun, a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Novelist quits rewrite about Republican puppet masters, perhaps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another
a rewrite produces a new version, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A writer gives up on revising a book about Republicans who secretly pull the strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppet masters' suggests political string-pullers, fitting the Republican surface, but means those who work dummies; 'perhaps' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventriloquists operate dummies and speak through them, so they are one kind of puppet handler.

clue.text: A politician with one excuse for failure

parts.note: taken as written
Lib is short for a Liberal politician
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician, as usual, has a ready excuse for things going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, an alibi is any pretext offered to avoid blame when something has gone wrong.

clue.text: Sad effort forming compromises

indicators.note: forming means shaping into something new, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A feeble attempt ends in unsatisfying concessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade-offs are balanced concessions in which one gain is accepted at the price of another loss.

clue.text: Support place in south-east for church tower

indicators.note: placing one thing in another means the first goes inside the second

parts.note: the compass abbreviation
a golf tee supports the ball
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Someone needs to find a spot in the south-east of the country for a church tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a tall tower, usually topped with a spire, rising from a church.

clue.text: Gatecrash popular event finally getting bawdy

parts.note: what is in is fashionable or popular

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of event
rude jokes are bawdy ones

explanation.surface: Uninvited guests barge in as a crowd-pleasing party turns raunchy at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to enter where you are not invited, which is to intrude.

clue.text: Examination of progress turning in quota by Bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to make progress

explanation.surface: A progress review looks at a quota set by a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which is why it carries a capital; here it is the verb meaning to put in the ground. The reversed piece goes inside the quota word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogation is a close questioning, a formal examination of someone.

clue.text: Reprimanded American's annoyed

definitions.meaning: second meaning: US slang for irritated

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the phrase means scolded; in American usage it means angry, hence the flag on the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both being given a telling-off and, in the US, being irritated or cross.

clue.text: Agreement accepted by rowing team makes a kind of sense

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing crew agreeing to something shows good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is vision, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Candy caught working with ferocity travelling around Newcastle area

indicators.note: working machinery is switched on, the usual crossword sense of operating

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: being around something means enclosing it
travelling things move about, so the letters change places

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
the letters to be rearranged
Newcastle is in the north-east of England, NE

explanation.surface: Someone caught selling sweets is set upon fiercely on a trip around Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged ferocity letters wrap around the north-east abbreviation, splitting after their sixth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery is the general word for sweets, which Americans call candy.

clue.text: Facial hair (not black) on strange part of body

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: a beard is facial hair
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A beard that isn't black sits oddly on someone's body.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear, a part of the human body.

clue.text: Middle of masthead below boom

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the central two letters of masthead
under means below

explanation.surface: On a ship, the centre of the mast-top sits beneath a boom.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical surface makes 'boom' look like a spar on a sailing ship; it is a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is a deep resounding noise, a boom.

clue.text: Head of strategy manages fields

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of strategy
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A head of strategy runs the playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Scopes are ranges or areas of activity, in the sense of fields of study.

clue.text: Believe singer holding monkey is a better bargain

indicators.note: holding something means having it enclosed in your grasp

parts.note: Cher had a huge hit with the song Believe
an ape is a primate like a monkey

explanation.surface: A singer clutching a monkey is trying to convince someone it is a better bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Believe' reads as a verb but is the title of Cher's 1998 hit, identifying the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheaper costs less, so it is more of a bargain than the alternative.

clue.text: Money lenders more certain to be found in America

indicators.note: to be found in a place is to be located inside it

parts.note: the abbreviation for the United States
surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A claim that lenders who are more confident are typically based in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurers lend money at excessive interest, so they are a kind of money lender.

clue.text: Chuck out timeless fabric

indicators.note: read as time-less, it says the fabric word goes without its time letters

parts.note: a textile is a woven fabric
the time part of this word is T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Throw away some ageless cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' splits into time and less, and both of the time letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, forcing them out of their country.

clue.text: Took the lead from sanctimonious individual left holding drug

parts.note: pi is informal for piously self-righteous

indicators.note: holding something means having it enclosed in your grasp

parts.note: one is a single individual
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
red signifies the political left

explanation.surface: A self-righteous person on the left, carrying drugs, led the way.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a British informal short form of pious. The drug letter sits between the individual and the political colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer something is to be first to develop it, to take the lead.

clue.text: Throw a loop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hurl or toss
second meaning: a strap or band hung to support something

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a lasso instruction, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for flinging something and a noun for a looped strap, such as one supporting an injured arm.

clue.text: Regularly snaffled cash box

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Somebody habitually pinches the cash box.
explanation.walkthrough: Snaffled is British slang for grabbed or stole.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a strong lockable container for money and valuables.

clue.text: Steersman sorted out disordered situation

indicators.note: sorting things out puts them in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A helmsman fixed a chaotic state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that 'sorted out' sits next to the definition of a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a hopelessly confused or messy state of affairs.
